_doc: THE ACT SPEC — PLAN_v6 PACKAGE 3a, DATA PINS OUT OF THE ENGINE. Driven by `tools/land lever`. THIS ACT MOVES ZERO VALUES: the board prediction here IS the board the tree already carries, and that equality is the standing falsifier (G1 / process law P1). The ONE identity that moves is engine_head, because the act edits engine/rl_after/_merged_recover.py to take six pin literals out of it — which is the effect 3a exists to produce, stated the other way round: engine_head moves if and only if CODE changed, so a future SHEET update, now a data commit, must not move it.
_doc_coherent_base: THE LAST COHERENT BASE — the prereg commit, immediately before the engine edit, where expected_boot.engine_head still equals md5(_merged_recover.py). It names the commit the PRE-TRANSACTION SELF-TEST's sandbox worktree is cut from, AND NOTHING ELSE: no prediction, no identity, no gate and no carrier of this act reads it, and the lander under test is the working copy either way. WHY IT IS NEEDED: process law P9 forces this act's engine edit into its own commit ahead of the landing, so between that commit and this landing the tree is incoherent BY DESIGN — the engine file has moved and its pin has not, which is exactly the restamp this landing performs. The self-test's practice landings are declared NO-OP rehearsals; their contract step asserts manifest-and-tree agreement on engine_head and would halt on the mid-act tree. Supervisor ruling 2026-08-21: 'The lander self-test proves THE LANDER, not the act. It therefore runs on a COHERENT tree.'

This act moves no value, touches no dial, no threshold and no data the board is made of; it moves where three pinned FACTS ABOUT AN INPUT are written down. prereg._doc_kill_switch: null — there is no dial to declare. A kill-switch leg answers 'what does the board look like with this change off', and the answer here is 'the same board', which is what board_before == board_after already asserts. commit_message:
PACKAGE 3a LANDED — THE SHEET PINS ARE OUT OF THE ENGINE. Board b3e8da99bc7f632e5d1eebc732f9cf01 BYTE-IDENTICAL; the only identity that moves is engine_head, because the act edited code.

PLAN_v6 PACKAGE 3a, of the sequence the owner locked in on 2026-08-20 (register v801, verbatim:
"Lock in the plan also, we can commence it after these fixes are done and the partially completed
initiatives that we're waiting on this are finished").

WHAT MOVED. The three pinned facts about the owner's injury/sitter sheet — md5, row count,
injured=Y count — were SIX LITERALS IN TWO DUPLICATED BLOCKS of engine/rl_after/_merged_recover.py:
O41_INJ_MD5/ROWS/Y at ORDER 41 and _SHEET_MD5/ROWS/Y at ORDER 42. They are now ONE DECLARATION in
data/sheet_pins.json, read by both blocks through _sheet_pins(). A sheet update is therefore a DATA
COMMIT, and engine_head moves if and only if CODE changed.

WHAT DID NOT MOVE, WHICH IS MOST OF IT. A drifted sheet still HALTS the build, fail-closed, with the
ORDER 41 and ORDER 42 halt text byte-unchanged; an ABSENT or MALFORMED declaration halts too
(SHEET-PIN HALT). EACH GUARD KEEPS ITS OWN FIRING REGIME — the pins are resolved INSIDE the dial's
own branch, so a build with RL_O41_INJ or RL_O42 off reads the declaration not at all, exactly as it
read the literals not at all before, and ORDER 41 still HALTS FIRST. PLAN_v6 3a is explicit that
unifying the two guards' halt behaviour would change semantics in the exact regime the collapse
proofs exercise, so it was not done. Proof: GUARD_REGIME_PROOF.txt, 18 checks, 18 PASS —
structural (AST: the reads are inside each dial's branch), textual (every halt fragment byte-equal
to the pre-edit file; every pinned value byte-equal to the literal it replaced), functional (the
loader halts on absent, malformed, holed and re-pointed declarations).

IN THE SAME ACT, AS 3a REQUIRES: docs/runbooks/R23_RUNBOOK.md gains ERRATUM E7. Its "move six
literals in two engine blocks in one commit with the sheet" instruction was made WRONG by this act
and a manual advance in the 3a->2b window would have followed it. E7 replaces it with the correct
procedure, states EXPLICITLY that the amended manual path is the INTERIM WRITER of
data/sheet_pins.json until `land round` (PACKAGE 2b) takes over as SOLE writer, and writes in the
review-forcing step a data commit still owes: PREREG-LITE — predicted sheet md5 + row and injured=Y
counts + disclosed movers, committed WITH the data change. The interim-writer RULE's durable home is
the pin file's own header and the engine's _sheet_pins() header; the runbook repeats it, because a
runbook is a procedure and not a law's home — this one needed five errata inside a single round.

THE ENUMERATED CHURN (G1), and nothing outside it: the engine edit, data/sheet_pins.json, one
carriers.py entry registering it as a lever carrier, the runbook amendment, this evidence directory,
and — written by THIS TRANSACTION, not hand-walked — the engine_head restamp in data/expected_boot.json
and data/release_contract.json, the contract re-seal, and the two board-view bundles that carry the
engine stamp. The store b745002eb0a0fbb1c34fa44f1ef708d6 is byte-unmoved and claimed as such;
as_of_round is HELD at 23; no column and no lineage entry are owed because the board did not move.

DECLARED, NOT SILENTLY SKIPPED (prereg section 8): the RULEBOOK line PLAN_v6 3a also asks for is NOT
written — law 10(a) makes any RULEBOOK change an owner-only word and none covers this act — and the
manifest-checked carrier FIELDS are not added. Both are reported as remaining 3a scope.
